skill.name: safe-refactor
skill.description: Refactor in small, verified steps, with behavior locked by tests before any change. Use when asked to refactor, clean up, rename, extract or restructure code without changing behavior.
skill.summary: Guide behavior-preserving refactors with baseline tests, small changes, dependency checks, and explicit verification.
skill.author: agentkitco

content.user_title: Refactor Code with Tests and Small Changes
content.value_statement: Code cleanup can introduce behavior changes that are difficult to detect. This skill guides small refactoring steps with baseline tests, dependency checks, and repeated verification.
actual_capabilities: Defines the refactoring goal and boundaries before editing code.
Directs baseline test runs and records pre-existing failures.
Guides characterization tests for behavior that lacks coverage.
Checks callers, dependents, documentation, and configuration before renaming symbols.
Separates changes into small steps with tests and type checks or lint after each step.
Reports completed work, verification results, excluded changes, and remaining uncertainty.
limitations: Provides workflow instructions rather than a bundled refactoring engine or test runner.
Depends on the host assistant and project tools to inspect, edit, and test code.
Tests cannot prove preservation of behavior they do not exercise.
Requires user input for unclear failures, public API breaks, or discovered bugs.

use_cases.title: Clean Up a Working Module
use_cases.description: Extract duplicated logic while preserving outputs, error messages, logging, and edge cases through small, verified edits.

use_cases.title: Protect Legacy Behavior
use_cases.description: Add characterization tests before restructuring code that lacks coverage, and document behavior that remains unverified.

use_cases.title: Review a Shared API Rename
use_cases.description: Identify callers and dependents before renaming exported symbols, and request approval when compatibility requires a breaking change.

prompt_templates.title: Assess a Refactoring Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Use safe-refactor to assess [module]. State the goal, behavior boundaries, existing tests, and baseline results before proposing any edits.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: establish scope and verification before changing code.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Repeated Logic
prompt_templates.prompt: Use safe-refactor to extract repeated logic in [file]. Preserve behavior, make one change per step, and run relevant tests after each step.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: reduce duplication in code with existing tests.

prompt_templates.title: Characterize Untested Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Use safe-refactor on [legacy module]. Add characterization tests for realistic inputs before restructuring. Preserve current errors and ordering, and report coverage gaps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: establish a safety net for legacy code.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Shared Symbol Rename
prompt_templates.prompt: Use safe-refactor to rename [exported symbol]. Check all callers and dependents, propose a deprecation path, and request approval before any API break.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate a compatibility-sensitive change across dependent code.

output_examples.input: Extract duplicated validation from two functions without changing their behavior.
output: Boundary: preserve validation order, error messages, and return values.
Baseline: relevant tests passed before editing.
Change: extracted the shared validation logic in one reviewable step.
Verification: relevant tests and lint passed after extraction.
Left unchanged: an unrelated naming inconsistency.

output_examples.input: Restructure a legacy parser that has no tests.
output: Characterization tests added for representative valid and invalid inputs.
Baseline behavior recorded, including existing error messages.
Restructuring completed in separate, verified steps.
Uncertainty: large input performance was not exercised.
Observed bug reported separately and left unchanged.

best_practices: Define behavior boundaries and record baseline failures before editing.
Add characterization tests before restructuring untested behavior.
Review each small diff and verify that rollback preserves pre-existing user edits.
anti_patterns: Mixing refactoring with bug fixes, features, or dependency upgrades.
Continuing through failing tests instead of undoing the last step and reducing its scope.
Changing public APIs without approval or a deprecation path.

faq.question: What does this skill provide?
faq.answer: It provides a structured workflow for behavior-preserving refactoring, including test baselines, dependency checks, incremental edits, and a final report.

faq.question: What happens when the code has no tests?
faq.answer: The workflow calls for characterization tests that record current behavior before refactoring begins.

faq.question: Does it guarantee identical behavior?
faq.answer: No. Verification depends on test coverage and available checks, and the final report must identify behavior that remains uncertain.

faq.question: Can it fix bugs during a refactor?
faq.answer: It directs the assistant to report discovered bugs and handle fixes as separate changes.

faq.question: When does it ask for user input?
faq.answer: It asks when tests cannot run, baseline failures are unexplained, a public API break is needed, or a real bug is found.

faq.question: Does it require a specific programming language?
faq.answer: No specific language is required. The host assistant must use the existing project tests, type checker, or linter.
